coverage.summary: Authored six worked examples covering every distinct assessed representation method. All examples have separate editable prompts and solutions; solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. No relation-led calculation rows require phantom gutters. Diagrams preserve hidden answers, use black marks, explicit 10 pt ordinary labels and 8.5 pt ticks. Free-form TikZ expresses rays and bounded solution segments, which the supplied template parameters do not explicitly support. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged; mathematical re-audit and rendered visual acceptance were not performed.

examples.derivation: For x<-1, -1 is excluded and solutions lie left of -1: the open endpoint and left ray agree. For x≥2, 2 is included and solutions lie right of 2: the closed endpoint and right ray agree. This follows the source's endpoint and direction conventions.
The drawn endpoint is at -2, is filled, and the ray extends left. Therefore the represented set is x≤-2, matching the solution and the source's graph-reading method.

Exchanging sides in 0≤x gives x≥0, represented by a closed endpoint at 0 and a right ray. x≤0 has the same included boundary but a left ray. Positive values belong only to the first set, negative values only to the second, and 0 belongs to both.

The conjunction -1≤x and x<4 includes -1, excludes 4, and includes every value between them. The diagram correctly joins a filled endpoint at -1 to an open endpoint at 4, following the source's bounded-region exercises.
The segment extends from -2 to 1, with an open endpoint at -2 and a filled endpoint at 1. Thus x is greater than -2 and at most 1: -2<x≤1.

Reading -1≥x from x gives x≤-1. The supplied erroneous graph instead represents x>-1, so both endpoint inclusion and direction are wrong. The corrected filled endpoint at -1 and left ray represent x≤-1 exactly. Both diagnostic principles are taught in the cited source.

review.summary: All six distinct assessed methods are mapped and covered; all 28 exact assessment locators have mappings. The six new examples are mathematically correct, source-supported and within scope. Existing examples are empty. Prompts and solutions are separate, with no answer leakage or missing continuation gutters. Plain solution prose/math inherits the supplied blue styling; diagram marks remain black, with declared 10 pt ordinary labels and 8.5 pt ticks. Free-form TikZ is justified because the supplied template interface has no explicit ray or interval-segment parameters. No syllabus exception is needed. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited; final-size visual verification remains for the capture stage.
